readings.title: The Wine Cup of Wrath for the Nations
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH commands Yirmeyahu to serve the cup of His burning displeasure to the geopolitical powers of the earth.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 25:15] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl to me, <dq>“Take <dn>את</dn> this wine cup of wrath from <dn>My</dn> hand, and make all the nations, to whom <dn>I</dn> send you, drink it.</dq> [16] <dq>“And they shall drink, and shake, and go mad because of the sword that <dn>I</dn> am sending among them.”</dq> [17] I then took the cup from the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and made all the nations drink, to whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had sent me, [18] namely Yerushalayim and the cities of Yehuḏah, and its sovereigns, its heads, to make them a ruin, an object of astonishment, a hissing, and a curse, as it is this day; [19] Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, and his servants, and his heads, and all his people; [20] and all the mixed multitude, and all the sovereigns of the land of Uts, and all the sovereigns of the land of the Philistines – even Ashqelon, and Azzah, and Eqron, and the remnant of Ashdoḏ; [21] Eḏom, and Mo’aḇ, and the children of Ammon; [22] and all the sovereigns of Tsor, and all the sovereigns of Tsiḏon, and the sovereigns of the coastlands which are beyond the sea; [23] Deḏan, and Tĕma, and Buz, and all who are in the farthest corners; [24] and all the sovereigns of Araḇia and all the sovereigns of the mixed multitude who dwell in the wilderness; [25] and all the sovereigns of Zimri, and all the sovereigns of Ěylam, and all the sovereigns of the Medes; [26] and all the sovereigns of the north, far and near, one with another, and all the reigns of the earth which are on the face of the ground. Also the sovereign of Shĕshaḵ shall drink after them.

readings.title: The Controversy with the Nations
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH enters into judgment with all flesh, sending a great whirlwind and a devouring sword from the farthest parts of the earth.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 25:27] “And you shall say to them, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, <dq>“Drink, be drunk, and vomit! Fall and rise no more, because of the sword which <dn>I</dn> am sending among you.”</dq> ’ [28] “And it shall be, when they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, then you shall say to them, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“You shall drink!</dq> [29] <dq>“For look, <dn>I</dn> am beginning to bring evil upon the city which is called by <dn>My</dn> Name, and should you be entirely unpunished? You are not going unpunished, for <dn>I</dn> am calling for <dn>את</dn> a sword on all the inhabitants of the earth,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.’ [30] “And you shall prophesy against them all these words, and say to them, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> roars from on high, and utters <dn>His</dn> voice from <dn>His</dn> set-apart dwelling place. <dn>He</dn> roars mightily over <dn>His</dn> fold, a shout as those who tread the grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth. [31] “Tumult shall come to the ends of the earth, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has a controversy with the nations. <dn>He</dn> shall enter into judgment with all flesh. The wrong <dn>He</dn> shall give to the sword,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [32] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“See, evil is going forth from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind is raised up from the farthest parts of the earth.</dq> [33] <dq>“And in that day the slain of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be from one end of the earth even to the other end of the earth. They shall not be lamented, or gathered, or buried, for they are dung on the face of the ground.</dq>

readings.title: The Slaughter of the Shepherds
readings.subtitle: The corrupt leaders of the flock are commanded to wail as YeHoVaH ravages their pastures with His burning displeasure.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 25:34] <dq>“Howl, you shepherds, and cry! And roll yourselves in the ashes, you leaders of the flock! For the days of your slaughter and your scatterings are completed, and you shall fall like a choice vessel.</dq> [35] <dq>“And a place of refuge shall perish from the shepherds, and escape from the leaders of the flock.</dq> [36] <dq>“Hear the cry of the shepherds, and a wailing of the leaders of the flock, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is ravaging their pasture!</dq> [37] <dq>“And the pastures of peace shall be cut down because of the burning displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [38] <dq>“Like a lion <dn>He</dn> shall leave <dn>His</dn> hiding place, for their land shall become a waste because of the sword of oppressors, and because of <dn>His</dn> burning displeasure.”</dq>

readings.title: Dictating the Words of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Yirmeyahu instructs Baruḵ to record the divine warnings, offering Yehuḏah a chance to turn back and receive pardon.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 36:1] And it came to be in the fourth year of Yehoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, that this word came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [2] <dq>“Take a scroll and write on it <dn>את</dn> all the words that <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you against Yisra’ĕl, and against Yehuḏah, and against all the nations, from the day <dn>I</dn> spoke to you, from the days of Yoshiyahu even to this day.</dq> [3] <dq>“It could be that the house of Yehuḏah hears of all the evil which <dn>I</dn> plan to bring upon them, so that each one turns back from his evil way, and <dn>I</dn> shall pardon their crookedness and their sin.”</dq> [4] And Yirmeyahu called Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah. And Baruḵ wrote on a scroll from the mouth of Yirmeyahu, all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had spoken to him. [5] And Yirmeyahu commanded Baruḵ, saying, “I am shut up, I am unable to enter the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [6] “But you shall enter, and shall read from the scroll which you have written from my mouth, the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in the hearing of the people in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the day of fasting. And also read them in the hearing of all Yehuḏah who come from their cities. [7] “It could be that they present their supplication before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and they turn back, each one from his evil way. For great is the displeasure and the wrath that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken against this people.” [8] And Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah did according to all that Yirmeyahu the prophet commanded him, reading from the book the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Fast and the Reading
readings.subtitle: During a national fast, Baruḵ reads the words of Yirmeyahu in the upper courtyard, bringing the message to the ears of the people.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 36:9] And it came to be in the fifth year of Yehoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, in the ninth new moon, that they called a fast before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to all the people in Yerushalayim, and to all the people who came from the cities of Yehuḏah to Yerushalayim. [10] And Baruḵ read from the book the words of Yirmeyahu in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in the room of Gemaryahu son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard at the entry of the New Gate of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in the hearing of all the people. [11] And Miḵayehu son of Gemaryahu, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from the book, [12] And then he went down to the sovereign’s house, into the scribe’s room. And there all the heads were sitting: Elishama the scribe, and Delayahu son of Shemayahu, and Elnathan son of Aḵbor, and Gemaryahu son of Shaphan, and Tsiḏqiyahu son of Ḥananyahu, and all the heads. [13] And Miḵayehu told them all the words which he heard when Baruḵ read the book in the hearing of the people.

readings.title: The Fear of the Heads
readings.subtitle: The heads examine the scroll, recognizing the gravity of the words, and advise Yirmeyahu and Baruḵ to hide before they notify the sovereign.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 36:14] Then all the heads sent Yehuḏi son of Nethanyahu, son of Shelemyahu, son of Kushi, to Baruḵ, saying, “Take in your hand <dn>את</dn> the scroll from which you have read in the hearing of the people, and come.” So Baruḵ son of Nĕriyahu took the scroll in his hand and came to them. [15] And they said to him, “Sit down, please, and read it in our hearing.” Then Baruḵ read it in their hearing. [16] And it came to be, when they had heard all the words, that they looked at each other in fear, and said to Baruḵ, “We are certainly going to report all these words to the sovereign.” [17] And they asked Baruḵ, saying, “Please explain to us, how did you write all these words? From his mouth?” [18] And Baruḵ answered them, “From his mouth he spoke all these words to me, and I wrote them with ink in the book.” [19] Then the heads said to Baruḵ, “Go, hide, you and Yirmeyahu, and let no one know where you are.” [20] And they went to the sovereign, into the court. But they put the scroll in the room of Elishama the scribe, and told all the words in the hearing of the sovereign.

readings.title: The Defiant Burning of the Word
readings.subtitle: Sovereign Yehoyaqim rejects the divine warning, actively attempting to destroy the written record and silence the prophets.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 36:21] The sovereign therefore sent Yehuḏi to bring <dn>את</dn> the scroll, and he took <dn>את</dn> it from the room of Elishama the scribe. And Yehuḏi read it in the hearing of the sovereign and in the hearing of all the heads standing beside the sovereign. [22] And the sovereign was sitting in the winter house in the ninth new moon, with a fire burning on the hearth before him. [23] Then it came to be, when Yehuḏi had read three or four columns, that the sovereign cut <dn>את</dn> it with the scribe’s knife and threw <dn>את</dn> it into the fire that was on the hearth, until the entire scroll was burned in the fire that was on the hearth. [24] Yet the sovereign and all his servants who heard all these words were not afraid, nor did they tear their garments. [25] Moreover, Elnathan, and Delayahu, and Gemaryahu pleaded with the sovereign not to burn the scroll, but he did not listen to them. [26] And the sovereign commanded Yeraḥme’ĕl son of the sovereign, and Serayahu son of Azri’ĕl, and Shelemyahu son of Aḇde’ĕl, to seize Baruḵ the scribe and Yirmeyahu the prophet, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had hid them.

readings.title: The Scroll Restored and the Curse Issued
readings.subtitle: The divine word is rewritten and expanded, issuing a severe judgment upon the rebellious sovereign and his descendants.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 36:27] And after the sovereign had burned the scroll with the words which Baruḵ had written from the mouth of Yirmeyahu, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu, saying, [28] <dq>“Take another scroll, and write on it <dn>את</dn> all the former words that were in the first scroll which Yehoyaqim the sovereign of Yehuḏah has burned,</dq> [29] <dq>and say to Yehoyaqim sovereign of Yehuḏah, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “You have burned <dn>את</dn> this scroll, saying, ‘Why have you written in it that the sovereign of Baḇel is certainly coming to destroy this land, and cause man and beast to cease from here?’ ”</dq> [30] <dq>Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning Yehoyaqim sovereign of Yehuḏah, “<dn>He</dn> shall have no one to sit on the throne of Daviḏ, and his dead body is to be thrown out, to the heat of the day and the frost of the night.</dq> [31] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall punish him, and his seed, and his servants for their crookedness. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring on them, and on the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and on the men of Yehuḏah all the evil <dn>I</dn> have spoken against them. But they did not listen.” ’ ”</dq> [32] So Yirmeyahu took another scroll and gave it to Baruḵ the scribe, son of Nĕriyahu, who wrote on it from the mouth of Yirmeyahu all the words of the book which Yehoyaqim sovereign of Yehuḏah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.

readings.title: A Prize of Life for Baruḵ
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH addresses Baruḵ's weariness, assuring him that while the systemic architecture is broken down, his life will be preserved.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 45:1] The word that Yirmeyahu the prophet spoke to Baruḵ son of Nĕriyah, when he had written these words in a book from the mouth of Yirmeyahu, in the fourth year of Yehoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying, [2] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, concerning you, Baruḵ: [3] You have said, “Woe to me now! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has added grief to my pain. I have been wearied with my sighing, and I have found no rest.” ’ [4] “Say this to him, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, what <dn>I</dn> am breaking down, and what <dn>I</dn> have planted <dn>I</dn> am plucking up, that is, <dn>את</dn> the entire land.</dq> [5] <dq>“And do you seek great matters for yourself? Do not seek them, for look, <dn>I</dn> am bringing evil on all flesh,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> your life to you as a prize in all places, wherever you go.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Rout at the River Euphrates
readings.subtitle: The army of Pharaoh Neḵo is stricken with fear and beaten down by the forces of Baḇel.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 46:1] The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which came to Yirmeyahu the prophet concerning the nations: [2] For Mitsrayim, concerning the army of Pharaoh Neḵo, sovereign of Mitsrayim, which was by the River Euphrates in Karkemish, and which Neḇuḵaḏretstsar the sovereign of Baḇel had stricken in the fourth year of Yehoyaqim, son of Yoshiyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah: [3] <dq>“Prepare <dn>את</dn> the large and the small shield, and draw near to battle!</dq> [4] <dq>“Harness <dn>את</dn> the horses, and mount up, you horsemen! Stand with helmets, polish the spears, put on the armour!</dq> [5] <dq>“Why do <dn>I</dn> see them afraid, turned back? And their fighters are beaten down. And they have fled in haste, and did not look back, for fear was all around,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [6] <dq>Do not let the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape. They shall stumble and fall toward the north, by the River Euphrates.</dq>

readings.title: A Day of Vengeance for the Master
readings.subtitle: Mitsrayim's attempt to surge like a flood is met with divine slaughter, leaving no healing for her wounds.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 46:7] <dq>Who is this rising like a flood, whose waters surge about like the rivers?</dq> [8] <dq>Mitsrayim rises like a flood, and its waters surge about like the rivers. And he says, ‘Let me rise and cover the earth; let me destroy the city and its inhabitants.’</dq> [9] <dq>Go up, O horses, and rage, O chariots! And let the mighty men go forth – Kush and Put who handle the shield, and Luḏ who handle and bend the bow.</dq> [10] <dq>For this is the day of the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, a day of vengeance, to revenge <dn>Himself</dn> on <dn>His</dn> adversaries. And the sword shall devour, and be satisfied and made drunk with their blood. For the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts has a slaughtering in the land of the north by the River Euphrates.</dq> [11] <dq>Go up to Gil’aḏ and take <dn>את</dn> balm, O maiden, the daughter of Mitsrayim. In vain you have used many remedies, there is no healing for you.</dq> [12] <dq>Nations have heard of your shame, and your cry has filled the land. For the mighty has stumbled against the mighty, they have both fallen together.</dq>

readings.title: The Appointed Time Missed
readings.subtitle: Neḇuḵaḏretstsar's coming invasion causes the strong ones of Mitsrayim to stumble, as their sovereign proves to be nothing but empty noise.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 46:13] The word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Yirmeyahu the prophet, about the coming of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel, to strike <dn>את</dn> the land of Mitsrayim: [14] <dq>“Declare in Mitsrayim, and let it be heard in Miḡdol. And let it be heard in Noph and in Taḥpanḥes. Say, ‘Stand fast and be prepared, for a sword shall devour all around you.’</dq> [15] <dq>“Why were your strong ones swept away? They did not stand because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> drove them away.</dq> [16] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> made many stumble; indeed, they fell over each other, and said, ‘Arise! Let us go back to our own people, and to the land of our birth, away from the oppressing sword.’</dq> [17] <dq>“There they cried, ‘Pharaoh, sovereign of Mitsrayim, is but a noise. <dn>He</dn> has let the appointed time pass by!’</dq> [18] <dq>“As <dn>I</dn> live,”</dq> declares the Sovereign, whose Name is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“For as Taḇor is among the mountains, and as Karmel by the sea, he shall come.</dq> [19] <dq>“O you daughter dwelling in Mitsrayim, prepare yourself to go into exile! For Noph shall become a waste and a ruin, and be burned, without inhabitant.</dq>

readings.title: The Forest Cut Down
readings.subtitle: The hired forces of Mitsrayim flee before the countless army of the north, bringing shame upon the daughter of Mitsrayim.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 46:20] <dq>“Mitsrayim is like a very pretty heifer, but destruction comes, it comes from the north.</dq> [21] <dq>“Her hired ones too, in her midst, are like fattened calves, for they too shall turn, they shall flee away together. They shall not stand, for the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment.</dq> [22] <dq>“Its sound moves along like a serpent, for they move on like an army and come against her with axes, like woodcutters.</dq> [23] <dq>“They shall cut down her forest,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“for it is not searched, because they are more numerous than locusts, and without number.</dq> [24] <dq>“The daughter of Mitsrayim shall be put to shame. She shall be given into the hand of the people of the north.”</dq>

readings.title: Punishment for Mitsrayim, Preservation for Ya’aqoḇ
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH guarantees the salvation of His servant Yisra’ĕl, promising a return to rest and a measured reproof in perfect justice.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 46:25] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, has said, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing punishment on <dn>את</dn> Amon of No, and on <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh, and on <dn>את</dn> Mitsrayim, and on <dn>את</dn> their mighty ones, and on <dn>את</dn> their sovereigns, and on <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh and on <dn>את</dn> those trusting in him.</dq> [26] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel and into the hand of his servants. And afterward it shall be inhabited as in the days of old,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [27] <dq>“But as for you, do not fear, O <dn>My</dn> servant Ya’aqoḇ, and do not be discouraged, O Yisra’ĕl! For look, <dn>I</dn> am saving you from afar, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. And Ya’aqoḇ shall return, and shall have rest and be at ease, with no one disturbing.</dq> [28] <dq>“Do not fear, O Ya’aqoḇ <dn>My</dn> servant,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“for <dn>I</dn> am with you. Though <dn>I</dn> make a complete end of all the nations to which <dn>I</dn> have driven you, yet <dn>I</dn> do not make a complete end of you. But <dn>I</dn> shall reprove <dn>את</dn> you in right-ruling, and by no means leave you unpunished.”</dq>
